Computer Science: We investigate a graph neural network for detecting anomalous network traffic. The proposed architecture learns node representations from communication patterns and classifies malicious connections. Experiments compare precision and recall against support vector machines and random forests on a network intrusion benchmark.
Electrical Engineering: This study presents a low-power CMOS amplifier for wireless communication receivers. A new biasing circuit reduces power consumption while maintaining gain and noise performance. Circuit simulations evaluate bandwidth, linearity, and stability under different supply voltages.
Psychology: This study examines the relationship between sleep quality and working memory in university students. Participants completed a cognitive task and questionnaires measuring stress and sleep habits. Regression analysis assessed whether perceived stress moderated the association between sleep duration and memory performance.
Mechanical Engineering: We study heat transfer and pressure loss in a compact heat exchanger using computational fluid dynamics. Different fin geometries are evaluated under turbulent flow conditions. The analysis compares thermal efficiency and pumping power to identify a suitable design for industrial cooling systems.
Civil Engineering: This study evaluates the seismic response of reinforced concrete buildings with different structural configurations. Finite element models are subjected to earthquake ground motions. Interstory drift and damage patterns are compared to assess the effectiveness of shear walls in improving structural performance.
Medical Science: We evaluate an intervention for improving glycemic control in adults with diabetes. Participants were followed for six months and assessed for changes in HbA1c, treatment adherence, and adverse events. Clinical outcomes were compared between the intervention and usual-care groups.
Biochemistry: We investigate the catalytic mechanism of an enzyme involved in cellular metabolism. Site-directed mutagenesis and kinetic assays identify residues essential for substrate binding. Protein structure analysis reveals how changes in the active site alter enzyme activity and molecular interactions.
